excerpts.speaker: Logan Endow
excerpts.short_exact_quote: I am adamantly against widening highways and I fully support a moratorium on road/highway widening.
excerpts.claim_summary: Endow unconditionally opposes highway widening and supports a road/highway-widening moratorium so transportation funds can shift to mass transit and complete streets.
excerpts.notes: Direct answer to the shared Bikemore highway-widening question.

excerpts.notes: Direct answer to the shared Bikemore highway-widening question.

excerpts.claim_summary: Boyce supports halting widening projects while officials review pedestrian and road safety and design transit-oriented alternatives; her answer does not specify a permanent ban.

comparisons.interpretation: Endow and Elizabeth Embry both oppose additional highway widening. Their answers share the no-widening proposition; differences in surrounding climate, safety, review, or project-specific rationale are matters of emphasis, not opposition.

Endow endorses a general highway-widening moratorium and redirecting investment to mass transit and complete streets. Boyce supports halting widening projects specifically while conducting safety review and designing transit-oriented alternatives; her answer does not establish a permanent moratorium.

Endow explicitly supports a general road/highway-widening moratorium. Benbow opposes several named expansion projects and rejects new highway construction, but does not expressly support a general moratorium covering all widening of existing roads; the overlap is narrower than a shared moratorium position.
